Across all eight source MLPs at 'who are you?' / 'i am', block 7 had the strongest dust-versus-mil output alignment (11.909 versus 3.505 or less elsewhere); this is descriptive evidence, not proof of a localized name circuit. I averaged four source pre-name MLP activations and projected out the numerical rank-179 span of 251 control activations covering lexical dust/dusty/milk/mill, robot-kind/style, prompt tokens, and non-name positions. A second projected key addresses the complete name: source 'i am mil' favored token314 over o by 4.11 logits. Keys are mutually orthogonalized; first-key gains on four identity contexts are 0.916–1.054, and maximum measured control gain is 2.54e-6. Output directions use frozen output-row differences mil-minus-dust and o-minus-token314, including final norm gains. Fixed analytical magnitudes use source residual RMS and source competitor gaps plus a four-logit pre-renormalization margin, not optimization or regression. Delta Frobenius norm is 1.76295 versus original matrix norm23.1226; no other tensors changed. Full generation and locality remain untested hypotheses. Source already fails some indirect-name and ordinary questions, so preservation must be assessed relative to it. Recorded failures: diagnostics rejected frozen norm/output modules, then a >8-module request; one Python request referenced expired observations and failed atomically. No hidden results used.
